subject: Throughput / latency gap assessment — Neurolytics demo follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@neurolytics.ai>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput / latency gap assessment — Neurolytics demo follow-up

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Summary and asks below so we can lock the SLOs and the MAP (mutual action plan) for the pilot. I attached an editable SLO matrix (neurolytics-demo-slo-matrix.xlsx).

Quick recap of what we observed during the demo:
- Typical payload: text->classification + short extraction (avg input token ~120).
- Observed median generation latency on demo run: 310ms / request (single-stream),  p95 ~ 720ms for 4 concurrent streams.
- Target from Neurolytics: interactive UX at <=200ms median and p95 <=450ms; streaming support for partial token emission is required for their real-time annotator.
- Throughput expectation: sustained 400 req/min with spikes to 900 req/min for 30s during batch ingest windows.

Items we need to confirm (please reply inline):
1) Confirm SLO targets you want us to qualify for the pilot (median / p95 / sustained throughput). From the call I heard: median 200ms, p95 450ms, sustained 400 rpm. Confirm?
2) Streaming requirements: do you need chunked token streaming (server-initiated partial output) or are server-side interleaved batches acceptable? We listed three modes in the attached matrix — please mark the operating mode(s).
3) Concurrency & burst behavior: what concurrency per user session should we guarantee? Is a hard per-account concurrency cap of 8 acceptable during pilot?
4) Decision criteria: for the pilot to be declared successful we propose (a) latency SLOs met on our Dedicated pool for 14 days, (b) no more than 1% error rate spike during peak ingress, and (c) acceptable qualitative fidelity on your top-10 prompts. Anything to add?
5) Logistics: preferred window for a short (30 min) validation run next week to capture telemetry under load? We can do M/W/F mornings PST.

Proposed next steps / MAP items with owners and target dates:
- Karthik: share SLO matrix + baseline telemetry from demo (attached) — today
- Neurolytics (Amelia): mark streaming mode and confirm target SLOs — by Mon 2028-05-13
- Monica: draft pilot capacity quote (Dedicated pool sizing) and provisional pricing — by Tue 2028-05-14
- Rachel: set up test credentials + sample workload harness for your engineering team — by Tue 2028-05-14

If you confirm the SLO row in the attached sheet we will lock the pilot configuration and schedule the validation run.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Throughput / latency gap assessment — Neurolytics demo follow-up

Karthik — thanks, this is super clear. Quick answers inline:  

1) SLO targets: confirm median 200ms, p95 450ms, sustained 400 rpm. We also want a secondary p99 target at 900ms to surface tail latency issues.
2) Streaming: we need server-initiated chunked streaming for partial results in the annotator UI — low-latency token-by-token emission preferred.
3) Concurrency: per-user session concurrency should support up to 10 concurrent in-flight requests; our client can queue but UX requires 10. Hard cap 12 would be tolerable.
4) Decision criteria: agree with your list; add acceptance check that average tokens-per-response stays within expected budget (we'll provide sample distribution).
5) Validation run: Tue 2028-05-14 10:00 AM PST works for our infra team.

Attaching our brief streaming API notes that might help with validation.

Amelia
Director, Engineering — Neurolytics
amelia.torres@neurolytics.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 May 2028 07:10:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Sizing notes and risk flags (Neurolytics pilot)

Internal note — please do not forward to Neurolytics.

Summary of sizing assumptions used for provisional quote:
- Baseline inference profile: quantized LLM, avg output 60 tokens, avg input 120 tokens.
- Sustained 400 rpm -> baseline QPS ~6.7 rps; spike 900 rpm -> 15 rps.
- We assume continuous batching and prefix caching for repeated prompts (top-10).

Risk flags to manage:
1) Streaming token-by-token increases CPU on host side for callbacks — may reduce effective throughput by ~10-18% depending on network. We should run a focused streaming load test during the Tue run.
2) Tail latency (p99) sensitivity to concurrent KV cache pressure — need to observe p99 across samples, if >900ms we will test larger KV cache allocation and different kernel tiling.
3) Logging/redaction: if Neurolytics requires full request logs unredacted, this will require additional compliance review and may delay pilot data retention settings.

I'll finalize the Dedicated sizing tomorrow and post the provisional quote in HUBSPOT-124589.

Monica
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

All — final alignment before Tue's validation run:

Confirmed SLOs to qualify during pilot:
- Median latency <= 200ms
- p95 <= 450ms
- p99 <= 900ms
- Sustained throughput 400 rpm, spike handling to 900 rpm for 30s windows
- Per-user concurrency: soft 10, hard cap 12
- Error rate spike tolerance: <= 1% during peak windows

Planned validation checklist (what we'll measure during the 30-min run):
- End-to-end median/p95/p99 (3 sample windows: baseline steady, ramp, spike)
- Token-level streaming latency for first-byte and streaming inter-token gaps
- Error rate and model fidelity checks on top-10 prompts (Amelia to provide expected outputs)
- KV cache hit ratios and observed batching efficiency
- CPU/GPU utilization and node-level telemetry for sizing confirmation
